echo: We spend too much time convincing buyers on sales calls.
hook: “If we get them on a call, we’ll close them” isn’t a flex. It’s booking you fewer calls and hurting your close rate.
h1: Estelle used to spend hours in LinkedIn DMs to book 3 sales calls a month. Now she books {{3 a week}} and closes 75% of them.
context: Estelle Winsett is a former attorney who styles high-performing lawyers from court to cocktails. She had an engaged audience of 9,000+ women, but her buyers only saw the $5,000 price, her deep process and her clients’ transformations once they were already on a call.
before_what: Hours of back-and-forth in LinkedIn DMs
after_what: A Conversion Quiz™ on her profile, posts and talks
built_1: Put her Conversion Quiz™ on her profile, under every post and on a QR code at her talks, so quiz takers came in without her being in the DMs
built_2: Built her Contrarian POV™, “It’s not your body, it’s your clothes”, into the quiz so her take stuck
built_3: They see the $5,000 offer, her detailed process, and her Contrarian take from other stylists before they hop on a call with her
r0s: quiz takers book a call within 10 days
r1s: sales calls, up from 3 a month
why: the convincing no longer happens on the call. The moment someone books a call still unconvinced, you’ve already added 45 minutes of convincing to your calendar, and weeks of follow-ups to your sales cycle.
up_next: Next question: Where does most of your traffic or audience come from today?
quad: Moving the convincing from the sales call to before it is quadrant 3 of the Compounding Revenue Per Visitor™ OS.
